title: Double-booked
setting: Two meetings are scheduled in the same room at the same time.

lines.t: The big room is double-booked at eleven. Two teams, both confirmed.
Who booked first?
The finance review, three weeks ago.
Then they keep it. Can the other one move?
I can reschedule it to one o'clock or move it to the small room.
How many people?
Nine, so the small room would be tight.
Reschedule, then. Ask them, don't tell them.
I'll offer one and three and let them choose.
Perfect. And block out the room properly this time.

title: Nine steps to five
setting: An office coordinator proposes cutting an enrolment process.

lines.t: Enrolling one student takes nine steps and about twenty-five minutes.
With two hundred a month, that's a lot of hours.
Eighty-three. I asked one question about each step.
Which was?
Who reads this, and what happens if it doesn't exist?
And?
Two steps had no answer at all. The certificate template and the folder.
Nobody has opened those folders since 2023.
Exactly. And the spreadsheet and timetable can pull from one source.
Do it. Send me the new workflow on one page.

title: Two at eleven
setting: A manager has booked himself into the same hour twice.

lines.t: He's double-booked at eleven. Two different people, same slot.
Who booked the second one?
He did, from his phone, while he was sitting in the first meeting.
Of course he did. Which one do we reschedule?
The internal one. The client has driven from Sofia.
Offer the internal one three times rather than one. People say yes faster when they choose.
And his diary management in general?
Block out time on Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Nothing goes in there.
He'll fill it himself within a week.
Then block it out again, and tell him what happened at eleven o'clock today.

title: Did it arrive
setting: A contract has gone out and nobody has confirmed anything.

lines.t: Did the contract go out?
By courier yesterday, and by registered post this morning.
Both?
Both. Last time the courier lost one and nobody could prove anything.
Sensible. Did they acknowledge receipt?
Not yet. I'll ring them at eleven.
Then circulate the new policy to the whole office while you wait.
Which distribution list? The old one still has three people who left in spring.
Fix the list first, then send. The policy goes as an attachment, with a two-line memo in the email itself.
And the meeting on the 3rd?
You minute the meeting, I'll chair it. My out of office is on from Thursday, so anything urgent comes to you.

title: Everything is urgent
setting: A new assistant has been handed a list where every line is marked urgent.

lines.t: Everything on this list is marked urgent.
Then prioritise it yourself, because whoever wrote it didn't.
How?
Two questions. Who is waiting, and what stops if you don't do it?
The travel booking stops three people flying on Monday.
That's first. What's the turn around on the supplier forms?
Two days, they said, and I've chased them up twice.
Then they can wait until Thursday. Keep on top of the to-do list and the petty admin stops feeling like a wave.
I'm also covering for Petar next week.
Cover for him on the diary and the post. Leave the rest, and liaise with the finance team so they know who to ask.
Do I coordinate the induction as well?
That's a back office workflow and it's written down. Follow it, and change nothing in your first month.

title: The blue folder
setting: Where things are kept, and what happens to them afterwards.

lines.t: Where does a signed contract actually live?
Scanned into the filing system, and the hard copy in the blue folder.
Both?
Both. The scan is for finding things. The paper is for lawyers.
And when it's finished?
We archive it after two years. Nothing leaves this office without a date on it.
There's a stack of old payslips on the shelf.
That's confidential waste. You shred those, they never go in the paper bin.
Understood. And the new supplier list?
Use the template. Data entry into the spreadsheet, then somebody senior has to sign off a document like that before it goes anywhere.
And if somebody asks me later whether we still have it?
If it's on file you can say yes in ten seconds. Record keeping is only worth anything when finding things is fast.

title: We run out of paper on Fridays
setting: The stationery cupboard empties on the same day every week.

lines.t: We've run low on paper again.
It happens every Friday, which means somebody prints their whole week on a Friday.
Do I raise a purchase order?
For office supplies under a hundred leva, no. Over that, yes, and get it signed.
The printer on the second floor is making a noise.
Put in a maintenance request today. Otherwise it breaks on the morning of the audit.
And the stock take?
The 30th. Two people, one counting and one writing, and nobody counts their own cupboard.
What else counts as facilities?
Heating, the lift, the coffee machine, and anything anyone complains about twice.

title: The first ten minutes
setting: Monday morning at the front desk, with two new people starting.

lines.t: You're on reception on Monday morning.
What do I actually do?
Everyone who isn't staff has to sign in, take a visitor badge, and wait for somebody to come down.
Even when they're expected?
Especially then. Same rule for the client and for the man who fixes the coffee machine.
And the two new starters?
Their induction begins at nine. Badges, a tour, and where the fire exit is before anything else.
Should I give them the handbook?
Give them coffee and a laptop first. The handbook can wait until eleven.
So the first ten minutes is what they'll actually remember.

title: Munich on Tuesday
setting: Three people are flying and one of them is driving.

lines.t: Three people to Munich on Tuesday. Do I book travel for all of them together?
One booking, one reference. It's far easier when a flight is cancelled.
They want different return dates.
Then three bookings. Ask once, in writing, so nobody changes their mind on Monday.
What's the per diem for Germany?
Fifty euros a day, and they don't have to keep receipts for it.
Nikolay is driving.
Then he claims mileage rather than a train ticket. The rate is in the policy.
When are the expense reports due?
Within two weeks of coming back. After that finance asks me, I ask them, and everybody has forgotten.
